Its terrain is convenient and advantageous,
and to send troops from there against the feudal lords
is like pouring water from the high roof's eaves.
Now Qí,
has the riches of Lángyá and Jímò in the east,
the firmness of Tàishān in the south,
the barrier of the Zhuó River in the west,
and the benefits of the Bó Sea in the north.
Its territory spans two thousand lǐ,
with a million halberd-bearing troops,
separated by a thousand lǐ beyond,
Qí gains tenfold strength from two.
Thus, these are the two Qíns, east and west.
Unless they are your own sons or brothers,
none should be made kings over Qí."
Gāozǔ said:
"Well said."
He bestowed five hundred catties of gold.
More than ten days later,
he enfeoffed Hán Xìn as the Marquis of Huáiyīn,
and divided his territory into two states.
Gāozǔ said the general Liú Jiǎ had repeatedly achieved merit,
and made him the King of Jīng,
ruling over Huáidōng.
His brother Jiāo was made the King of Chǔ,
ruling over Huáixī.
His son Féi was made the King of Qí,
ruling over more than seventy cities,
and all people who spoke the Qí dialect belonged to Qí.
Then, assessing achievements,
he distributed tallies and carried out enfeoffments with the various marquises.
He moved the King of Hán, Xìn, to Tàiyuán.
In the seventh year,
the Xiōngnú attacked the King of Hán, Xìn, at Mǎyì,
and Xìn thus plotted rebellion in Tàiyuán.
Mǎnqiū Chén of Báitǔ and Wáng Huáng set up the former Zhào general Zhào Lì as king to rebel,
and Gāozǔ personally went to attack them.
It happened to be bitterly cold,
and two or three out of ten soldiers lost fingers to frostbite,
then they reached Píngchéng.
The Xiōngnú besieged our forces at Píngchéng,
and withdrew after seven days.
He ordered Fán Kuài to remain and pacify the Dài region.
He set up his elder brother Liú Zhòng as the King of Dài.
In the second month,
Gāozǔ passed through Zhào and Luòyáng from Píngchéng,
and arrived at Cháng'ān.
The Chánglè Palace was completed,
and the chancellor and below moved their administration to Cháng'ān.
In the eighth year,
Gāozǔ went east to attack the remaining rebels of the King of Hán, Xìn, at Dōngyuán.
Chancellor Xiāo was constructing the Wèiyāng Palace,
erecting the eastern gate tower, northern gate tower, front hall, armory, and great granary.
Gāozǔ returned.
Seeing the palace towers were extremely magnificent,
he grew angry,
and said to Xiāo Hé:
"The realm has been troubled by bitter warfare for years,
and success or failure is still uncertain,
why is the construction of palaces so excessive?"
Xiāo Hé said:
"The realm is not yet settled,
so we can take this opportunity to complete the palaces.
Moreover, the Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home,
if not magnificent and splendid, he cannot emphasize his majesty,
and also to prevent later generations from surpassing it."
Gāozǔ then was pleased.
When Gāozǔ went to Dōngyuán,
he passed by Bóren,
where the chancellor of Zhào, Guàn Gāo and others, plotted to assassinate Gāozǔ.
Gāozǔ's heart was stirred,
so he did not stay.
The King of Dài, Liú Zhòng, abandoned his state and fled,
returning on his own to Luòyáng,
and was demoted to be the Marquis of Héyáng.
In the ninth year,
the affair of the chancellor of Zhào, Guàn Gāo and others, was discovered,
and their three clans were exterminated.
The King of Zhào, Áo, was demoted to be the Marquis of Xuānpíng.
That year,
the noble families of Chǔ—Zhāo, Qū, Jǐng, Huái—and the Tián clan of Qí were moved to Guānzhōng.
The Wèiyāng Palace was completed.
Gāozǔ held a grand court assembly for the feudal lords and ministers,
and set a feast in the front hall of Wèiyāng.
Gāozǔ raised a jade cup,
stood up to toast Tàishàng Huáng,
saying: "Originally, father often considered me a ne'er-do-well,
unable to manage property,
not as capable as Zhòng.
Now, whose achievements are greater, mine or Zhòng's?"
All the ministers in the hall shouted "Long live the Emperor,"
and laughed joyfully.
In the tenth year, tenth month,

the King of Huáinán, Qíng Bù; the King of Liáng, Péng Yuè; the King of Yān, Lú Wǎn; the King of Jīng, Liú Jiǎ; the King of Chǔ, Liú Jiāo; the King of Qí, Liú Féi; and the King of Chángshā, Wú Ruì, all came to court at the Chánglè Palace.
Spring and summer passed without incident.
In the seventh month,
Tàishàng Huáng passed away in the Lìyáng Palace.
The Kings of Chǔ and Liáng all came to attend the funeral.
Prisoners in Lìyáng were pardoned.
Lìyì was renamed Xīnfēng.
In the eighth month,
the chancellor of Zhào, Chén Xī, rebelled in the Dài region.
The Emperor said:
"Xī once served as my envoy,
and was very trustworthy.
The Dài region is of urgent importance to me,
so I enfeoffed Xī as a marquis,
and made him chancellor to guard Dài.
Now he joins Wáng Huáng and others in plundering the Dài region!
The officials and people of Dài are not guilty;
let them be pardoned."
In the ninth month,
the Emperor personally went east to attack him.
He reached Hándān.
The Emperor said joyfully:
"Xī does not hold Hándān to the south and block the Zhāng River,
I know he can do nothing."
Hearing that Xī's generals were all former merchants,
the Emperor said:
"I know how to deal with them."
Then he lured Xī's generals with much gold,
and many of Xī's generals surrendered.
In the eleventh year,
while Gāozǔ was at Hándān, before the execution of Xī and others was complete,
Xī's general Hóu Chǎng led over ten thousand troops roving,
Wáng Huáng stationed his army at Qūnì,
and Zhāng Chūn crossed the river to attack Liáochéng.
Hàn sent General Guō Méng to attack together with the Qí generals,
and they greatly defeated them.
Grand Commandant Zhōu Bó entered via the Tàiyuán route,
and pacified the Dài region.
Reaching Mǎyì,
Mǎyì did not surrender,
so he attacked and destroyed it.
Xī's general Zhào Lì guarded Dōngyuán,
and Gāozǔ attacked it,
but could not take it.
After over a month,
the defenders cursed Gāozǔ,
and Gāozǔ was enraged.
When the city surrendered,
he ordered those who had cursed him to be beheaded,
and pardoned those who had not.
Thus, a division was made in the north of Zhào Mountain,
and Zǐ Héng was established as the King of Dài,
with his capital at Jìnyáng.
In the spring,
Huáiyīn Marquess Hán Xìn plotted rebellion in Guānzhōng,
and his three families were exterminated.
In the summer,
Liáng King Péng Yuè plotted rebellion,
and was deposed and relocated to Shǔ;
he again sought to rebel,
and thus his three families were exterminated.
Zǐ Huī was established as the King of Liáng,
and Zǐ Yǒu as the King of Huáiyáng.
In the autumn, the seventh month,
Huáinán King Qíng Bù rebelled,
annexing the territory of Jīng King Liú Jiǎ to the east,
and crossed the Huái River to the north,
causing Chǔ King Jiāo to flee to Xuē.
Gāozǔ personally went to attack him.
Zǐ Cháng was established as the King of Huáinán.
In the twelfth year, in October,
Gāozǔ had already engaged Bù's army at Huìzhuì,
where Bù fled,
and he ordered other generals to pursue him.
Gāozǔ returned,
passing by Pèi,
and stayed.
He held a banquet in Pèi Palace,
summoning all the old friends, elders, and younger generations to indulge in drinking,
gathering one hundred and twenty young men from Pèi,
whom he taught to sing.
Drunk with wine,
Gāozǔ beat a zhu,
composing lyrics himself, saying:
“The great wind rises, clouds fly aloft,
power spreads over the land, returning to my homeland,
how can I obtain valiant men to guard the four corners!”
He ordered the youths to all accompany him in song.
Gāozǔ then rose to dance,
his emotions stirred,
and tears streamed down his face.
He spoke to Pèi Gōng's brother, saying:
“A traveler longs for his homeland.
Although I reside in Guānzhōng,
even if a thousand ages pass, my soul will fondly think of Pèi.
Since as Pèi Gōng, I punished the wicked and rebellious,
thereby securing the whole realm,
let Pèi be my place of bathing,
restore its people,
and for generations do not assign it. ”
The fathers, brothers, and old mothers of Pèi and the old friends reveled in joyous drinking,
speaking of old times to amuse and delight.
After more than ten days,
Gāozǔ wished to leave,
but the fathers and brothers of Pèi earnestly requested him to stay.
Gāozǔ said:
“I have many people with me,
and the fathers and brothers cannot provide for them.”
Thus he left.
The whole county of Pèi went west to press him with gifts.
Gāozǔ thus stayed again,
and entertained for three more days.
The fathers and brothers of Pèi all knelt, saying:
“Pèi is fortunate to have been restored,
but Fēng has not yet been restored,
we only beg Your Majesty's compassion.”
Gāozǔ said:
“Fēng is where I was born and raised,
it's not that I forget it,
but it once revolted against me with Yōng Chǐ joining Wèi.”
The fathers and brothers of Pèi earnestly requested,
so Fēng was also restored,
treated the same as Pèi.
At this point, Liú Pì was appointed as the King of Wú.
Hàn's generals separately attacked Bù’s army south and north of the Tǎo River,
and they were all greatly defeated,
with Bù pursued and killed at Póyáng.
Fán Kuài was a separate general set to stabilize Dài,
and Chén Xī was executed at Dāngchéng.
In November,
Gāozǔ returned from Bù’s army to Cháng’ān.
In December,
Gāozǔ declared:
“The First Emperor of Qín, Hidden King of Chǔ Chén Shé, King of Wèi Ānlí, King of Qí Mín, and King of Zhào Dàoxiāng all have no descendants,
instruct to guard their tombs with ten families each,
twenty families for the Qín Emperor,
and five families for Wèi Prince Wújì.”
Grant amnesty to the officials and people of the Dài region who were plundered by Chén Xī and Zhào Lì,
who are all pardoned.
Chén Xī’s surrendered generals proclaimed that, when Xī rebelled,
Yān King Lú Wǎn sent envoys to Xī,
and conspired secretly.
The ruler sent Bì Yáng Hóu to summon Wǎn,
but Wǎn feigned illness.
Bì Yáng Hóu returned,
fully reporting that Wǎn's rebellion had true beginnings.
In February,
Fán Kuài and Zhōu Bó were sent to lead troops to attack Yān King Wǎn.
Pardon those officials and people of Yān who revolted.
Crown Prince Jiàn was established as the King of Yān.
When Gāozǔ attacked Bù,
he was struck by a stray arrow,
and fell ill upon the road.
His illness became severe,
and Lǚ Hòu sought an excellent physician.
The doctor came in for an audience,
and Gāozǔ questioned the doctor.
The doctor said:
“The illness is treatable.”
Then Gāozǔ mocked and cursed him, saying:
“I was a commoner who took ten thousand states with a three-foot sword,
is this not Heaven’s decree?
Life and death lie with Heaven,
what use are you even if you were Biǎn Què?”
He refused treatment,
gifted him fifty jin of gold, and dismissed him.
Later, Lǚ Hòu asked:
“After a hundred years, Your Majesty,
when Chancellor Xiāo dies,
whom shall you appoint to replace him?”
The ruler said:
“Cáo Cān is suitable.”
Asked for the next in line,
the ruler said:
“Wáng Líng is suitable.
However, Líng is somewhat stubborn,
Chén Píng can assist him.
Chén Píng’s intelligence is surplus,
yet difficult to rely upon alone.
Zhōu Bó is strong and steady but has little culture,
however, Liu's safety lies with Bó,
and he can be made Grand Commandant.”
Lǚ Hòu inquired further about the future,
the ruler said:
“Thereafter is beyond your understanding.”
Lú Wǎn, with several thousand cavalry, waited at the border, observing,
hoping for his recovery to return and offer thanks.
On Jiǎchén in the fourth month,
Gāozǔ passed away in Chánglè Palace.
For four days, mourning was not initiated.
Lǚ Hòu conspired with Shěn Shíqí, saying:
“The generals were once commoners alongside the Emperor,
now they are subjects, facing north,
they often harbor resentment,
now they must serve a young sovereign,
if not completely purged,
the realm will not be at peace.”
Someone heard this,
and informed General Lì.
General Lì went to see Shěn Shíqí,
saying:
“I heard the Emperor has passed,
yet four days have not seen mourning,
with plans to execute the generals.
If this is true,
the realm is in danger.
Chén Píng and Guàn Yīng command one hundred thousand, guarding Xíngyáng,
Fán Kuài and Zhōu Bó lead two hundred thousand to pacify Yān and Dài,
if they hear of the Emperor’s death,
and that all generals are executed,
they will surely unite forces, return home, and attack Guānzhōng.
Ministers inside revolt,
feudal lords outside rebel,
destruction can come in the blink of an eye.”
Shěn Shíqí went in and reported this,
thus, on Dīngmǐ, mourning was initiated,
and a general amnesty was declared for the realm.
Upon hearing of Gāozǔ's passing,
Lú Wǎn fled to the Huns.
On Bǐngyín,
the burial took place.
On Jǐsì,
the Crown Prince ascended,
arriving at the Supreme Ancestor's Temple.
All the ministers said:
“Gāozǔ rose from obscurity,
restored order from chaos, reverses the disordered world,
pacified the realm,
and became the Grand Ancestor of Hàn,
his achievements are supreme.”
His title was honored as High Emperor.
The Crown Prince succeeded the title as Emperor,
known as Emperor Xiàohuì.
It was decreed that the prefectures and feudal lords each establish a temple for Gāozǔ,
to offer sacrifices according to the seasons.
In the fifth year of Emperor Hui's reign,
recalling Emperor Gaozu's joy and sorrow in Pei,
he made the Pei Palace the original temple of Emperor Gaozu.
The one hundred and twenty singing boys taught by Emperor Gaozu
were all ordered to perform wind music.
If any were missing later,
they were promptly replaced.
Emperor Gaozu had eight sons:
the eldest, born of a concubine, was Qí Dàohuìwáng Féi;
next was Emperor Hui,
son of Empress Lǚ;
next was Zhào Yǐnwáng Rúyì, son of Lady Qī;
next was Dàiwáng Héng,
who was later established as Emperor Wén,
son of Empress Dowager Bó;
next was Liángwáng Huī,
who during Empress Dowager Lǚ's time was transferred to become Zhào Gòngwáng;
next was Huáiyángwáng Yǒu,
who during Empress Dowager Lǚ's time was transferred to become Zhào Yōuwáng;
next was Huáinán Lìwáng Cháng;
next was Yānwáng Jiàn.
The Grand Historian says:
The governance of the Xià dynasty was characterized by loyalty.
The flaw of loyalty
was that the petty people became crude,
so the Yīn people succeeded it with reverence.
The flaw of reverence
was that the petty people became superstitious,
so the Zhōu people succeeded it with refinement. The flaw of refinement,
was that the petty people became superficial,
so to remedy superficiality, nothing is better than loyalty.
The ways of the Three Dynasties seem to cycle,
ending and beginning anew.
Between the Zhōu and Qín dynasties,
it can be said that refinement had become flawed.
The governance of Qín did not change this,
but instead intensified harsh laws and punishments.
Was this not erroneous?
Thus, when Hàn arose,
it inherited the flaws and implemented changes,
keeping the people from weariness,
and attained the mandate of Heaven.
The court held its assemblies in the tenth month.
His carriage and robes featured a yellow canopy and leftward banner.
He was buried at Chánglíng.
Empress Dowager Lǚ
was Emperor Gaozu's consort from his humble days,
and gave birth to Emperor Hui and the daughter Lǔyuán Tàihòu.
When Emperor Gaozu became King of Hàn,
he obtained Lady Qī from Dìngtáo,
loved and favored her,
and she gave birth to Zhào Yǐnwáng Rúyì.
Emperor Hui was benevolent and weak by nature,
and Emperor Gaozu considered him unlike himself.
He often wished to depose the Crown Prince
and establish Lady Qī's son Rúyì,
as Rúyì resembled him.
Lady Qī, being favored,
often accompanied the Emperor east of Hánguān Pass,
weeping day and night,
wishing to have her son replace the Crown Prince.
Empress Lǚ was older,
often left to guard the capital,
rarely saw the Emperor,
and grew increasingly distant.
After Rúyì was established as King of Zhào,
he nearly replaced the Crown Prince several times.
Thanks to the ministers' protests
and the strategies of Liúhóu,
the Crown Prince was not deposed.
Empress Lǚ was a person of firm resolve,
assisted Emperor Gaozu in pacifying the realm,
and many of the executed ministers were due to Empress Lǚ's efforts.
Empress Lǚ had two elder brothers,
both of whom were generals.
The eldest brother, Zhōulǚhóu, died in service,
and his son Lǚ Tái was enfeoffed as Lìhóu,
and his son Lǚ Chǎn as Jiāohóu;
the second brother Lǚ Shìzhī was enfeoffed as Jiànchénghóu.
In the twelfth year of Emperor Gaozu, on the jiǎchén day of the fourth month,
he passed away in the Chánglè Palace,
and the Crown Prince succeeded to the title of Emperor.
At that time, Emperor Gaozu had eight sons:
the eldest son Féi,
older brother of Emperor Hui,
from a different mother,
was King of Qí;
the rest were all younger brothers of Emperor Hui:
Lady Qī's son Rúyì was King of Zhào,
Lady Bó's son Héng was King of Dài,
the various consorts' sons: Huī was King of Liáng,
Yǒu was King of Huáiyáng,
Cháng was King of Huáinán,
Jiàn was King of Yān.
Emperor Gaozu's younger brother Jiāo was King of Chǔ,
and his elder brother's son Bì was King of Wú.
Among non-Liú meritorious officials, the son of Fānjūn Wú Ruì, Chén, was King of Chángshā.
Empress Dowager Lǚ deeply resented Lady Qī and her son, the King of Zhào.
She then ordered Lady Qī imprisoned in the Yǒngxiàng,
and summoned the King of Zhào.
The messenger returned three times,
as the Zhào Chancellor, Jiànpínghóu Zhōu Chāng, said to the messenger:
"Emperor Gaozu entrusted the King of Zhào to my care.
The King of Zhào is young.
I have privately heard that the Empress Dowager resents Lady Qī
and wishes to summon the King of Zhào to execute them together.
I dare not send the King.
Moreover, the King is ill
and cannot obey the summons."
Empress Dowager Lǚ was greatly angered,
and then sent someone to summon the Zhào Chancellor.
When the Zhào Chancellor was brought to Cháng'ān,
she then sent someone again to summon the King of Zhào.
The King came,
but had not yet arrived.
Emperor Hui, being kind and benevolent,
knew the Empress Dowager was angry.
He personally went to meet the King of Zhào at Bàshàng,
entered the palace with him,
and personally kept the King of Zhào by his side for daily life and meals.
The Empress Dowager wished to kill him,
but found no opportunity.
In the twelfth month of the first year of Emperor Hui's reign,
the Emperor went out hunting early in the morning.
The King of Zhào, being young,
could not rise early.
When the Empress Dowager heard he was alone,
she sent someone with poisoned wine for him to drink.
At daybreak,
when Emperor Hui returned,
the King of Zhào was already dead.
Thereupon, she transferred Huáiyángwáng Yǒu to be King of Zhào.
In summer,
an edict was issued posthumously bestowing upon Lìhóu's father the title Lìngwǔhóu.
The Empress Dowager then cut off Lady Qī's hands and feet,
gouged out her eyes,
burned her ears,
made her drink a potion that rendered her mute,
and placed her in a latrine,
naming her a "human swine."
After several days,
she summoned Emperor Hui to view the human swine.
When Emperor Hui saw it,
he asked,
and then realized it was Lady Qī.
He then wept bitterly,
fell ill from the shock,
and for over a year could not rise.
He sent someone to say to the Empress Dowager:
"This is not something a human would do.
I, as your son,
am ultimately unfit to govern the realm."
From then on, Emperor Hui drank daily and indulged in dissipation,
neglecting governance,
and thus remained ill.
In the second year,
Chǔ Yuánwáng and Qí Dàohuìwáng both came to court.
In the tenth month,
Emperor Hui and the King of Qí feasted before the Empress Dowager.
Emperor Hui, considering the King of Qí his elder brother,
placed him in the seat of honor,
following the etiquette of family.
The Empress Dowager was angered,
and then ordered two cups of poisoned wine to be poured,
placed before them,
and commanded the King of Qí to rise and offer a toast.
The King of Qí rose,
and Emperor Hui also rose,
taking a cup intending to toast together.
The Empress Dowager then became alarmed,
and personally rose to spill Emperor Hui's cup.
The King of Qí found this strange,
and thus did not dare drink,
pretending to be drunk and leaving.
Upon inquiry,
he learned it was poisoned.
The King of Qí was terrified,
thinking he would not escape Cháng'ān,
and grew anxious.
The Qí Interior Secretary Shì advised the King, saying:
"The Empress Dowager has only Emperor Hui and Princess Lǔyuán.
Now, you, King, possess over seventy cities,
while the Princess only has a few cities for her sustenance.
If you sincerely offer one commandery to the Empress Dowager
as a bathing fief for the Princess,
the Empress Dowager will surely be pleased,
and you, King, will have no worries."
Thus, the King of Qí ascended to the prefecture of Chéngyáng,
honoring the princess as the Empress Dowager.
Lǚ Hòu was pleased,
and consented.
Then they held a banquet at the Qí residence,
enjoying drinking,
and when it ended,
they returned the King of Qí.
In the third year,
they began constructing the city of Cháng'ān,
halfway completed by the fourth year,
and completed by the fifth and sixth years.
They invited marquises to gather.
In October, they attended court to celebrate.
In the autumn of the seventh year, on the wǔ-yín day of the eighth month,
Emperor Xiào Huì passed away.
Mourning was announced,
and the Empress Dowager cried,
yet her tears did not fall.
Zhang Bìqiáng, the son of Liú Hóu, became an attendant,
at the age of fifteen,
and said to the Chancellor:
“The Empress Dowager only had Xiào Huì,
now he has passed,
but she cries without sadness.
Do you know why?”
The Chancellor said:
“What is the reason?”
Bìqiáng said:
“The Emperor had no strong sons,
and the Empress Dowager feared you all.
If you now request to appoint Lǚ Tái, Lǚ Chǎn, and Lǚ Lù as generals,
to command soldiers in the southern and northern armies,
and allow various Lǚs to enter the palace,
to participate in affairs,
thus the Empress Dowager will be at ease,
and you all may escape disaster.”
The Chancellor then followed Bìqiáng’s plan.
The Empress Dowager was pleased,
and her crying became sorrowful.
The power of the Lǚ clan arose from this point.
A general amnesty was then declared throughout the land.
On the xīnchǒu day of September,
the burial took place.
The Crown Prince ascended to become Emperor,
and visited the temple of Gāo.
In the first year,
all orders came from the Empress Dowager.
The Empress Dowager styled herself as the regent,
and planned to establish the various Lǚs as kings,
consulting the Right Chancellor, Wáng Líng.
Wáng Líng said:
“Emperor Gāo made an oath with the sacrifice of a white horse saying, 'If any non-Liú clan becomes king,
all under heaven will attack them.'
To now make the Lǚs kings,
is not in accordance with the covenant.”
The Empress Dowager was displeased.
She consulted the Left Chancellor Chén Píng and Marquis of Jiàng, Zhōu Bó.
Bó and others replied:
“Emperor Gāo pacified the realm,
and made his kin kings,
now the Empress Dowager rules,
making her brothers, the various Lǚs, kings,
nothing is impossible.”
The Empress Dowager was pleased,
and dismissed the court.
Wáng Líng reproached Chén Píng and the Marquis of Jiàng, saying:
“At first, with Emperor Gāo, we made a blood oath,
weren’t you all present?
Now Emperor Gāo has passed,
leaving a female ruler,
wanting to make the Lǚs kings,
you all follow her desires, flattering her, and breaking the covenant,
with what face will you meet Emperor Gāo below?”
Chén Píng and the Marquis of Jiàng said:
“To argue openly in court now,
we are not as good as you;
but to preserve the state,
and ensure the succession of the Liú clan,
you are not as good as us.”
Wáng Líng had no response.
In November,
the Empress Dowager wished to dismiss Wáng Líng,
so she appointed him Imperial Tutor,
stripping him of his chancellor's authority.
Wáng Líng then was ill and retired home.
She then appointed Left Chancellor Píng as Right Chancellor,
and Pì Yáng Hóu Shěn Shíqí as Left Chancellor.
The Left Chancellor did not manage affairs,
allowing him to oversee the palace,
as if he were the Charioteer.
Shíqí was favored by the Empress Dowager,
and often handled matters,
public ministers made decisions following his direction.
She then posthumously honored the father of Lì Hóu as the Prince of Dàowǔ,
intending to gradually promote the Lǚs to kingship.
In April,
the Empress Dowager wanted to make the Lǚs marquises,
so she first ennobled the minister of merit from the time of Gāozǔ, Wúzé, as Marquis of Bóchén.
The Princess Lǔ Yuán passed away,
granted the posthumous title of Lady Dowager Lǔ Yuán.
Her son Yǎn was made King of Lǔ.
The father of King Lǔ,
was the Marquis of Xuānpíng, Zhāng Áo.
The son of Qí Dàohuì King Zhāng was made Marquis of Zhūxū,
marrying Lǚ Lù’s daughter.
Chancellor of Qí, Shòu, was made Marquis of Píngdìng.
The Lesser Treasurer Yán was made Marquis of Wú.
Then Lǚ Zhòng was made Marquis of Pèi,
Lǚ Píng was made Marquis of Fúliǔ,
Zhāng Mǎi was made Marquis of Nángōng.
The Empress Dowager wished to make the Lǚs kings,
first elevating Jiàng, son of Xiào Huì's harem, as King of Huáiyáng,
and Bù Yí as King of Chángshān,
and Zhī Shān as Marquis of Xiàngchéng,
and Zhāo as Marquis of Zhǐ,
and Wǔ as Marquis of Húguān.
The Empress Dowager hinted to the great ministers,
and the ministers requested to make Lì Hóu Lǚ Tái as King of Lǚ,
which the Empress Dowager permitted.
Jiànchēng Kānghou Shìzhī passed away,
his successor was guilty of crimes,
and was stripped of his title,
choosing his brother Lǚ Lù as Marquis of Húlíng,
continuing the lineage of Marquis Kāng.
In the second year,
King of Chángshān passed away,
replacing him with his brother, Marquis of Xiàngchéng, Shān as King of Chángshān,
changing his name to Yì.
In November,
King Lǚ Tái passed away,
posthumously named Sù Wáng,
his son Jiā succeeded as king.
In the third year,
nothing significant happened.
In the fourth year,
Lǚ Xū was made Marquis of Línguāng,
Lǚ Tā as Marquis of Yú,
Lǚ Gēngshǐ as Marquis of Zhùqí,
Lǚ Fèn as Marquis of Lǚchéng,
and five chancellors of the marquises.
During the time when the daughter of the Marquis of Xuānpíng was Empress Xiào Huì,
she had no children,
pretended to be pregnant,
took the child of a beautiful woman, and named it her own,
killed his mother,
and established her named son as Crown Prince.
When Xiào Huì passed,
the Crown Prince became Emperor.
When the Emperor matured,
he learned that his mother had died,
and he was not truly the Empress's child,
and thus declared:
“How could the Empress kill my mother and name me?
I am not yet grown,
when I am, I will act.”
The Empress Dowager heard and was worried,
fearing he would rebel,
thus imprisoned him in the depths of the palace,
claiming the Emperor was very ill,
and left him unseen.
The Empress Dowager said:
“To rule the world and govern for the people,
should be like the heavens,
embracing them like the earth,
with joy above to bring peace to the people,
and the people cheerfully serving their rulers,
joy and harmony bring governance to the world.
Now the Emperor has been ill and not recovered,
becoming vague and disordered,
unable to carry on the ancestral sacrifices,
unfit to bear the world,
he must be replaced.”
All ministers bowed their heads and said:
“The Empress Dowager considers deeply for the peace of the temple and state,
the ministers bow their heads and obey the decree.”
The Emperor was deposed,
and the Empress Dowager imprisoned and killed him.
On the bǐngchén day of May,
Chángshān King Yì was made Emperor,
renamed to Hóng.
Not naming it the first year because,
the Empress Dowager controlled the affairs of the world.
Zhǐ Hóu Zhāo became King of Chángshān.
The office of Tàiwèi was established,
with the Marquis of Jiàng, Bó, as Tàiwèi.
In the eighth month of the fifth year,
the King of Huáiyáng passed away,
replaced by his brother, Marquis of Húguān, Wǔ as King of Huáiyáng.
In the tenth month of the sixth year,
the Empress Dowager said that King Lǚ Jiā was living arrogantly,
and deposed him,
replaced by Lǚ Chǎn as King of Lǚ, the brother of Sù Wáng Tái.
In the summer,
a general amnesty was declared across the empire.
Xīngjū, son of the Qi Dào Huì King, was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Dōngmóu.
In the seventh year, in the month of January,
the Grand Empress Dowager summoned King Yǒu of Zhào.
Yǒu had a daughter of the Zhū Lǚ clan as his queen,
but did not love her,
loving another concubine instead.
The daughter of the Zhū Lǚ clan was jealous,
became angry and departed,
slandering him to the Grand Empress Dowager,
falsely accusing him as guilty, saying,
"How can the Lǚ clan get a king!
After the Grand Empress Dowager is a hundred years old,
I will surely strike them."
The Grand Empress Dowager was furious,
and because of this, summoned King Zhào.
When King Zhào arrived,
he was stationed at a residence and not seen,
ordered to be surrounded by guards,
and not given food.
Some of his ministers secretly provided food,
but were immediately apprehended and judged.
King Zhào was starving,
and thus sang:
"The Zhū Lǚ are in power, and the Liú clan is in danger,
the princes and marquises are coerced to forcefully give me a bride.
My bride is jealous and accuses me of evil,
the slanderous woman disrupts the state, yet the superior is unaware.
Without loyal ministers, why abandon the state?
Resolve yourself in the wild fields, oh azure heaven, uphold justice!
Alas, it cannot be regretted, better to decide early.
To be a king and starve to death, who will show pity?
The Lǚ clan is devoid of reason, entrust revenge to heaven."
On the day of Dīngchǒu,
King Zhào died in confinement,
and was buried with the common rites among the people's graves in Cháng'ān.
On Jǐchǒu,
there was a solar eclipse,
and the day turned dark.
The Grand Empress Dowager detested it,
her heart was not pleased,
and thus she said to her attendants,
"This is because of me."
In the month of February,
Liáng King Huī was moved to become King Zhào.
Lǚ King Chǎn was transferred to Liáng,
but he did not visit his state,
serving as the Grand Tutor to the Emperor.
The Emperor's son, Píngchāng Marquis Tài was established as Lǚ King.
The name Liáng was changed to Lǚ,
and Lǚ was changed to Jìchuān.
The Grand Empress Dowager's daughter's sister Lǚ Xū had a daughter who was the wife of Yínglíng Marquis Liú Zé,
and Zé became Grand General.
Empress Dowager conferred royal status upon the Lǚ clan,
fearing after her demise the generals of the Liú family would cause harm,
thereby appointing Liú Zé as King of Lángyá,
to soothe his heart.
When Liáng King Huī was transferred to King Zhào,
he harbored unhappiness in his heart.
The Grand Empress Dowager gave a daughter of Lǚ Chǎn as Queen of King Zhào.
All the Queen's attendants were from the Zhū Lǚ clan,
wielding power,
secretly watching King Zhào,
making it impossible for him to act freely.
The King had a favored concubine,
whom the Queen had poisoned and killed.
The King then composed four odes,
and had them sung by musicians.
The King was sorrowful,
and in June he committed suicide.
When the Grand Empress Dowager heard of it,
she thought the King had abandoned the rituals of the ancestral temple for a woman,
and annulled his heir.
Xuānpíng Marquis Zhāng Áo died,
and his son Yǎn was made King of Lǔ,
Áo was posthumously awarded the title of Lǔ Yuán Wáng.
In the autumn,
the Grand Empress Dowager sent an emissary to inform the King of Dài,
intending to move him to Zhào.
The King of Dài apologized,
expressing a wish to defend the borders of Dài.
Grand Tutor Chǎn, Chancellor Píng, and others said,
"Wǔxìn Marquis Lǚ Lù should be given priority in rank,
and placed first,
please establish him as King Zhào."
The Grand Empress Dowager agreed,
posthumously honoring Lù’s father, Marquis Kāng, as Zhào Zhāo King.
In September,
Yān Líng King Jiàn died,
leaving a beautiful woman and child.
The Grand Empress Dowager sent someone to kill them,
leaving no heir,
and the state was abolished.
In the eighth year, in October,
Lǚ Sù King’s son, Dōngpíng Marquis Lǚ Tōng, was made King of Yān,
and Tōng's brother Lǚ Zhuāng was enfeoffed as Dōngpíng Marquis.
In the middle of March,
Lady Lǚ conducted a purification ceremony,
and on her return through Zhǐ Road,
she saw a creature resembling a blue dog,
grasping at her side,
but it suddenly vanished.
Divination was performed,
saying King Zhào Rúyì was causing misfortune.
Lady Lǚ then fell ill with a side injury.
Lady Lǚ, for the sake of her grandson Lǔ Yuán King Yǎn, who was young,
having lost his parents early,
being orphaned and weak,
thus enfeoffed two sons from the former concubine of Zhāng Áo,
Chǐ as Xīndū Marquis,
and Shòu as Lèchāng Marquis,
to assist Lǔ Yuán King Yǎn.
She also enfeoffed Central Grand Attendant Zhāng Shì as Jiànlíng Marquis,
and Lǚ Róng as Zhùzī Marquis.
Among the eunuchs, the administrators and ministers were all made Within-the-Passes Marquises,
with fiefdoms of five hundred households.
In the middle of July,
Lady Lǚ fell gravely ill,
and so she appointed King Zhào Lǚ Lù as Grand General,
to lead the northern army;
Lǚ King Chǎn commanded the southern army.
Empress Dowager Lǚ admonished Chǎn and Lù, saying,
"The Grand Emperor has already settled the empire,
and made an agreement with the great ministers,
saying,
'Whoever is king who is not of the Liú clan,
the world will unite to strike them.'
Now, since the Lǚ clan is enfeoffed,
the great ministers are not at peace.
If I should die,
the Emperor is young,
I fear the great ministers will rebel.
You must rely on military strength to guard the palace,
be careful not to conduct the mourning rites,
and do not allow others to control you."
On the day of Xīnsì,
Lady Lǚ passed away,
leaving a testament to bestow a thousand gold coins to each of the princes,
and to grant gold based on rank to all the generals, ministers, marquises, and officials.
A great amnesty was declared.
Lǚ King Chǎn was made Regent-Marshal,
and Lǚ Lù’s daughter became Empress.
After Lady Lǚ was buried,
Xīn Zuǒ Chancellor Shěn Shíqǐ was made Grand Tutor to the Emperor.
Zhūxū Marquis Liú Zhāng was courageous and powerful,
and Dōngmóu Marquis Xīngjū was his brother,
both were brothers of Qí Aī King,
residing in Cháng'ān.
At that time,
the Zhū Lǚ were in control, wielding power,
with intentions to create disorder,
but feared the former chief ministers of the Grand Emperor, Jiàng and Guàn,
and dared not act.
Zhūxū Marquis's wife,
a daughter of Lǚ Lù,
secretly knew of their plot.
Fearing execution,
she secretly sent someone to inform her brother, King Qí,
wanting him to raise troops in the west,
to execute the Zhū Lǚ and establish themselves.
Zhūxū Marquis wished to collaborate from within with the great ministers as a response.
King Qí wanted to mobilize troops,
but his minister objected.
On the day of Bǐngwǔ in August,
King Qí wanted to send someone to execute the Minister,
and Minister Zhào Píng then rebelled,
leading troops to surround the King,
and the King killed the Minister,
then mobilized forces to the east,
deceitfully seized the forces of King Lángyá,
and commanded them to move west.
The details are recorded in the “Account of King Qí.”
King Qí then sent letters to the princes, saying,
"The Grand Emperor pacified the empire,
and enfeoffed his sons and brothers,
appointing Dào Huì King as King of Qí.
After Dào Huì King passed away,
Emperor Xiàohuì ordered Left Minister Liú Hóu to establish me as King of Qí.
Emperor Hui of Hàn passed away,
and Empress Dowager Gāo took charge of governance.
Though advanced in years,
she listened to the various Lǚ family members,
arbitrarily deposed the emperor and installed another,
and furthermore successively killed three kings of Zhào,
eliminating Liáng, Zhào, and Yān to enfeoff the various Lǚ as kings,
and divided Qí into four parts.
Loyal ministers offered remonstrance,
but the Empress Dowager, being deluded and confused, would not listen.
Now that Empress Dowager Gāo has passed away,
and the emperor is young and in the prime of youth,
unable to govern the empire,
he must rely on the great ministers and feudal lords.
Yet the various Lǚ have presumptuously elevated their own offices,
gathered troops to enhance their authority,
coerced the marquises and loyal ministers,
and forged imperial decrees to command the empire,
thereby endangering the imperial ancestral temple.
I, the unworthy one, am leading troops to enter and execute those who improperly claim kingship."
When Hàn heard of this,
Chancellor of State Lǚ Chǎn and others dispatched Yǐngyīn Hóu Guàn Yīng to lead troops and attack him.
Guàn Yīng arrived at Xíngyáng,
and then plotted, saying:
"The various Lǚ hold military power within the passes,
intending to endanger the Liú family and establish themselves.
If I now defeat Qí and return to report,
this would only increase the resources of the Lǚ family."
So he remained encamped at Xíngyáng,
sending envoys to inform the King of Qí and the other feudal lords,
to form an alliance with them,
and await a change from the Lǚ family,
so they could jointly execute them.
When the King of Qí heard this,
he withdrew his troops to the western border to await the agreement.
Lǚ Lù and Lǚ Chǎn wanted to start a rebellion within the passes,
but internally they feared Jiàng Hóu, Zhūxū Hóu, and others,
externally they feared the troops of Qí and Chǔ,
and they also worried that Guàn Yīng would betray them.
They intended to wait until Guàn Yīng's troops joined with Qí's before acting,
and hesitated without reaching a decision.
At that time,
Jìchuān King Tài, Huáiyáng King Wǔ, and Chángshān King Cháo, who were nominally younger brothers of the young emperor,
as well as Lǔyuán King, the grandson of Empress Lǚ,
were all young and had not yet gone to their fiefdoms,
residing in Cháng'ān.
King of Zhào Lù and King of Liáng Chǎn each commanded troops stationed in the northern and southern armies,
and all were men of the Lǚ family.
The marquises and assembled ministers had no assurance of their own lives.
Grand Commandant Jiàng Hóu Zhōu Bó could not enter the army camps to take command of the troops.
Qūzhōu Hóu Lì Shāng was old and ill,
and his son Lì Jì was on good terms with Lǚ Lù.
Jiàng Hóu then plotted with Chancellor Chén Píng,
sending men to coerce Lì Shāng,
and ordering his son Lì Jì to go and deceive Lǚ Lù, saying:
"Emperor Gāo and Empress Lǚ together stabilized the empire,
and the nine kings established by the Liú family,
along with the three kings established by the Lǚ family,
were all decided by the deliberations of the great ministers,
and the matter had already been announced to the feudal lords,
who all considered it appropriate.
Now that the Empress Dowager has passed away,
and the emperor is young,
yet you bear the seal of the King of Zhào,
and instead of urgently going to your fiefdom to guard the borders,
you serve as a supreme general,
leading troops and remaining here,
arousing suspicion among the great ministers and feudal lords.
Why do you not return the general's seal,
and hand over the troops to the Grand Commandant?
Request that the King of Liáng return the seal of the Chancellor of State,
and after swearing an oath with the great ministers, go to your fiefdom.
Then the Qí troops will surely withdraw,
the great ministers will be at ease,
and you can rest easy and rule over a thousand lǐ,
which is an advantage for ten thousand generations."
Lǚ Lù believed this plan was sound,
and intended to return the general's seal,
handing over the troops to the Grand Commandant.
He sent someone to report to Lǚ Chǎn and the elders of the Lǚ family;
some considered it advantageous,
while others said it was not,
and the plan remained undecided due to hesitation.
Lǚ Lù trusted Lì Jì,
and often went out with him hunting.
Once, he visited his aunt Lǚ Xū,
who became greatly enraged,
saying: "If you, as a general, abandon the army,
the Lǚ family will now have no place left."
Then she brought out all her pearls, jades, and precious vessels, scattering them in the hall,
saying: "There is no need to guard them for others."
Left Chancellor Shíyī was dismissed.
On the morning of the gēngshēn day of the eighth month,
Píngyáng Hóu Zhú, acting as Grandee of the Censorate,
went to see Chancellor of State Chǎn to discuss matters.
The Chief of the Gentlemen-at-Arms Jiǎ Shòu, having returned from an embassy to Qí,
thereupon reproached Chǎn, saying:
"If the king does not go to his fiefdom early,
now even if he wishes to go,
can he still do so?"
He fully informed Chǎn about Guàn Yīng forming an alliance with Qí and Chǔ,
intending to execute the various Lǚ.
Then he urged Chǎn to quickly enter the palace.
Píngyáng Hóu overheard some of their conversation,
and swiftly reported it to the Chancellor and Grand Commandant.
The Grand Commandant wanted to enter the northern army,
but could not gain entry.
Xiāngpíng Hóu Tōng was in charge of the tally and credentials,
so he ordered him to take the credentials and falsely admit the Grand Commandant into the northern army.
The Grand Commandant again ordered Lì Jì and the Diplomat Liú Jiē to first persuade Lǚ Lù, saying:
"The emperor has ordered the Grand Commandant to take command of the northern army,
and wishes you to go to your fiefdom.
Quickly return the general's seal and take your leave.
If not,
disaster will soon arise."
Lǚ Lù believed that Elder Lì would not deceive him,
so he removed the seal and handed it to the Diplomat,
and surrendered the troops to the Grand Commandant.
The Grand Commandant, leading him into the army gate,
issued an order to the army, saying:
"Those for the Lǚ family, bare the right shoulder;
those for the Liú family, bare the left shoulder."
The entire army bared the left shoulder for the Liú family.
When the Grand Commandant arrived,
General Lǚ Lù had already removed the supreme general's seal and departed,
so the Grand Commandant then took command of the northern army.
However, there was still the southern army.
When Píngyáng Hóu heard of this,
he reported Lǚ Chǎn's plot to Chancellor Píng,
and Chancellor Píng then summoned Zhūxū Hóu to assist the Grand Commandant.
The Grand Commandant ordered Zhūxū Hóu to guard the army gate.
He ordered Píngyáng Hóu to inform the Commandant of the Guard:
"Do not allow Chancellor of State Chǎn to enter the palace gate."
Lǚ Chǎn did not know that Lǚ Lù had already left the northern army,
so he entered Wèiyāng Palace,
intending to start a rebellion.
He could not enter the palace gate,
and paced back and forth.
Píngyáng Hóu feared he could not prevail,
and swiftly informed the Grand Commandant.
The Grand Commandant still feared he could not overcome the various Lǚ,
and did not dare to openly declare their execution,
so he sent Zhūxū Hóu to tell him:
"Quickly enter the palace to guard the emperor."
Zhūxū Hóu requested soldiers,
and the Grand Commandant gave him over a thousand men.
Entering the gate of Wèiyāng Palace,
he then encountered Chǎn in the courtyard.
At the time of the late afternoon meal,
he then attacked Chǎn.
Chǎn fled.
A great wind arose in the sky,
causing his attendants to become disordered,
and none dared to fight.
They pursued Chǎn,
and killed him in the privy of the Chief of the Gentlemen-at-Arms' office.
After Zhūxū Hóu had killed Chǎn,
the emperor ordered a receptionist to take the credentials and reward Zhūxū Hóu.
Zhūxū Hóu wanted to seize the credential token,
but the receptionist refused.
Zhūxū Hóu then rode along with him in his carriage,
and using the credential token, galloped away,
beheading the Commandant of the Guards of Chánglè Palace, Lǚ Gēngshǐ.
Returning,
he galloped into the northern army,
and reported to the Grand Commandant.
The Grand Commandant rose,
bowed and congratulated Zhūxū Hóu, saying:
"The only worry was Lǚ Chǎn,
now that he has been executed,
the empire is settled."
Then he sent men to divide and fully arrest the men and women of the various Lǚ,
and all, regardless of age, were beheaded.
On the xīnyǒu day,
they captured and beheaded Lǚ Lù,
and flogged Lǚ Xū to death.
They sent men to execute Yān King Lǚ Tōng,
and deposed Lǔ King Yǎn.
On the rénxū day,
the emperor's Grand Tutor Shíyī was reappointed as Left Chancellor.
On the wùchén day,
Jìchuān King was transferred to be King of Liáng,
and the son of Zhào Yōu King, Suì, was established as King of Zhào.
They sent Zhūxū Hóu Zhāng to inform the King of Qí about the execution of the various Lǚ,
ordering him to withdraw his troops.
Guàn Yīng's troops also withdrew from Xíngyáng and returned.
The ministers conspired secretly, saying:
“The Young Emperor and Liáng, Huáiyáng, and Chángshān kings,
are not true sons of Xiào Huì.
Empress Lǚ deceitfully took another's child,
killed his mother,
raised him in the harem,
and made him Xiào Huì’s son,
establishing him as heir,
along with the other kings,
to strengthen the Lǚ clan.
Now that the Lǚs have been exterminated,
if we let these stand,
and they hold power long,
we will have no place.
It's better to choose the worthiest among the kings and establish him.”
Some said, “Qí Dào Huì Wáng, the eldest son of Gāodì,
his legitimate son is now King of Qí,
tracing the lineage,
he is Gāodì’s legitimate eldest grandson;
he can be established.”
The ministers all said:
“The Lǚs brought ruin to the ancestral temple with their vile external influence,
disturbing the meritorious ministers.
Now the Qí king's maternal family is Sì Jūn,
Sì Jūn
is a wicked man,
if we establish the Qí king,
it would be like the Lǚs again.”
They considered establishing the Huáinán king,
but thought him too young,
and his maternal family was also wicked.
Then they said:
“The Dài king is now the visible son of Gāodì,
the eldest,
benevolent, filial, and generous.
His maternal family, the Bó clan, is prudent and good.
Moreover, establishing the eldest is appropriate,
known for his benevolence and filial piety throughout the land—
this is convenient.”
Thus, they secretly sent someone to summon the Dài king.
The Dài king sent someone to decline courteously.
After refusing twice,
he finally traveled with six chariots.
On the last day of the ninth month, jǐyǒu,
he arrived in Cháng'ān,
staying at the Dài residence.
All the ministers went to pay respects,
presenting the emperor’s seal to the Dài king,
jointly honoring him as emperor.
The Dài king repeatedly declined,
but the ministers insisted,
and then he agreed.
Dōngmóu Hóu Xīngjū said:
“I contributed nothing to the extermination of the Lǚs,
may I be allowed to clear the palace?”
So with Tàipǔ Rǔyīn Hóu Ténggōng, he entered the palace,
and said to the Young Emperor:
“Your majesty is not of the Liú clan,
you should not be established.”
Then he directed the halberd guards to lay down arms and leave.
A few refused to lay down arms,
but eunuch Zhāng Zé persuaded them,
and they also disarmed.
Ténggōng summoned a carriage for the Young Emperor.
The Young Emperor asked: “Where are you taking me?”
Ténggōng replied: “To another residence.”
He was lodged at Shàofǔ.
They then procured the imperial carriage
to formally welcome the Dài king at his residence.
It was reported: “The palace is cleared.”
That night, the Dài king entered Wèiyáng Palace.
Ten attendant officials holding halberds guarded the front gate,
saying: “The emperor is here,
who are you entering?”
The Dài king explained to the Tàiwèi.
The Tàiwèi went to persuade,
and the ten attendants disarmed and left.
The Dài king then entered and took charge.
At night,
officers separately executed Liáng, Huáiyáng, and Chángshān kings and the Young Emperor at their residences.
The Dài king ascended as emperor.
He passed in the twenty-third year,
posthumously titled Emperor Xiào Wén.
Shǐjì Gōng said:
During Emperor Xiào Huì and Empress Gāo,
the common people escaped the miseries of the Warring States,
rulers and ministers all sought rest and non-action,
thus Emperor Huì ruled passively,
Empress Gāo ruled in his stead,
politics remained within the inner chambers,
and the world was peaceful.
Punishments were seldom used,
and criminals were few.
The people tended to agriculture,
and clothing and food prospered.
Emperor Xiào Wén,
was the middle son of Gāozǔ.
In the spring of the eleventh year of Gāozǔ,
after defeating Chén Xī’s army,
solidifying Dài territory,
he was designated Dài king,
residing in Zhōngdū.
He was the son of Empress Bó.
He reigned for seventeen years,
in the eighth year of Empress Gāo, seventh month,
Empress Gāo passed away.
In the ninth month,
Lǚ Chǎn and others intended rebellion,
endangering the Liú clan,
and ministers collectively exterminated them,
planning to invite the Dài king,
this is recounted in “Empress Lǚ.”
Chancellor Chén Píng and Tàiwèi Zhōu Bó dispatched someone to invite the Dài king.
The Dài king asked his attendants and Zhāng Wǔ.
Zhāng Wǔ and others deliberated:
“All the Han ministers were generals in the time of Gāodì,
proficient in military affairs,
cunning strategists,
their intentions surely extend beyond this,
only fearing the might of Gāodì and Empress Lǚ.
Now, with the Lǚs gone,
blood freshly spilled in the capital,
they claim to invite the king,
but it’s risky.
The king should feign illness and not go,
to observe the situation.”
Sòng Chāng opposed:
“The ministers' views are wrong.
Qin lost control,
warlords and strongmen rose,
countless believed they could seize power,
yet the throne ultimately belonged to the Liú,
who won the people’s allegiance,
that’s one.
Gāodì bestowed titles on his kin,
territories interlocking like canine teeth,
it’s a stable foundation,
admired by all,
that's two.
Han rose,
eradicated Qin's harsh laws,
simplified statutes,
extended virtue,
people found comfort,
resistant to disturbance,
that's three.
Despite Empress Lǚ’s temper,
placing her family in power,
the Tàiwèi entered the northern army with a token,
commanded loyalty to the Liú,
rejecting the Lǚs,
ultimately destroying them.
This was granted by heaven,
not human power.
Even if the ministers plot change,
commoners won’t follow,
can factionalism succeed?
Now within are Zhūxū, Dōngmóu kin,
outside fearing Wú, Chǔ, Huáinán, Lángyá, Qí, Dài’s strength.
The only sons of Gāodì are Huáinán and the king,
the king being elder,
virtuous, benevolent,
esteemed across the land,
so ministers seek you because of widespread sentiment,
no doubt, king.”
The Dài king consulted with the Empress,
yet was undecided.
Divining by tortoise shell,
the hexagram was “Great Harmony.”
It was interpreted:
“On the day gēng, I am heaven's king,
like Xià's Qǐ, brilliant.”
The Dài king remarked:
“I am already king,
how could I be another king?”
The soothsayer replied:
“This ‘heavenly king’ means the emperor.”
So the Dài king sent his uncle Bó Zhāo to Jiàng Hóu,
where Jiàng Hóu explained the rationale to invite the king.
Bó Zhāo reported back, saying:
“It's true,
there’s no doubt.”
The Dài king laughed, saying to Sòng Chāng:
“Indeed, as you said.”
He ordered Sòng Chāng to accompany him,
while Zhāng Wǔ and six others traveled to Cháng'ān.
Resting at Gāolíng,
Sòng Chāng was sent ahead to observe Cháng'ān.
Chāng arrived at the Wèi Bridge,
and all the chancellors and officials went out to welcome him.
Sòng Chāng reported back.
The King of Dài rode quickly to the Wèi Bridge,
where all the ministers paid homage and addressed him as lord.
The King of Dài disembarked from his carriage and paid his respects.
The Grand Marshal, Bó, stepped forward and said,
"May I request a private conversation?"
Sòng Chāng replied,
"If it is public business,
discuss it publicly.
If it is private,
a king should not accept private communications."
The Grand Marshal then knelt and presented the imperial seal and tally.
The King of Dài graciously replied,
"Let us discuss this at the Dài residence."
He then quickly entered the Dài residence.
The ministers followed him there.

The Chancellor Chén Píng, Grand Marshal Zhōu Bó, Grand General Chén Wǔ, Chief Censor Zhāng Cāng, Patriarch Liú Yǐng, Zhūxū Marquis Liú Zhāng, Dōngmóu Marquis Liú Xīngjū, and Court Official Liú Jiē all bowed twice and said:
"Zǐhóng and others are not Emperor Xiàohuì's sons,
they should not inherit the ancestral temple.
We respectfully sought the counsel of Hòu Liè, Marquis of Yīn'ān, and the King of Lángyá with the imperial clan, high officials, marquises, and officials of two thousand shi to deliberate:
'The Great King is the eldest son of Emperor Gāo.
He should be the successor of Emperor Gāo.'
We hope the Great King will ascend to the throne as the Son of Heaven."
The King of Dài replied:
"To uphold the ancestral temple of Emperor Gāo
is a weighty matter.
I am not naturally talented,
insufficient to bear the responsibility of the ancestral temple.
I wish to consult King Chǔ on what is appropriate,
I dare not take this upon myself."
The ministers all firmly requested him to accept.
The King of Dài declined thrice while facing west,
and twice while facing south.
Chancellor Píng and others said:
"In our humble judgment,
the Great King is most suitable to uphold the ancestral temple of Emperor Gāo.
Even the feudal lords and all the people of the world see it as fitting.
For the sake of the ancestral temple and the state,
we dare not ignore this.
We hope the Great King will kindly listen to us.
We humbly present the imperial seal and tally with a double bow."
The King of Dài said:
"If the imperial kin, generals, officials, marquises, and all agree that I am most suitable,
then I dare not refuse."
Thus, he ascended to the position of the Son of Heaven.
The ministers attended him with proper ceremonies.
Taìpù Yīng and Dōngmóu Marquis Xīngjū were dispatched to cleanse the palace,
preparing the ceremonial chariot,
and welcoming him to the Dài residence.
The Emperor entered the Weiyang Palace on the same day.
That night, Sòng Chāng was appointed as Guard General,
overseeing the northern and southern armies.
Zhāng Wǔ was made Chamberlain,
serving in the inner palace.
Then he sat in front of the main hall.
That night, an imperial edict was issued stating:
"Recently, the Lü clan wielded power arbitrarily,
plotted great treason,
and sought to endanger the ancestral temple of the Liú family.
Fortunately, the generals, officials, marquises, and the imperial kin exterminated them,
thus all deserved their punishment.
As I have just ascended to the throne,
I announce a general amnesty to the world,
awarding one noble rank to the people,
gifting cattle and wine to households of one hundred people,
and ordering a five-day feast."
(In the first year, tenth month, of Emperor Xiàowén,
Gēngxū day, Lángyá King Zé was reassigned as King of Yān.
On Xīnhài day,
the Emperor ascended the throne,
and paid respects at the Gāo ancestral temple.
Right Chancellor Píng was reassigned as Left Chancellor,
and Grand Marshal Bó became Right Chancellor.
Grand General Guàn Yīng was appointed as Grand Marshal.
The lands seized by the Lü from Qí and Chǔ,
were all restored to them.
On Rénzǐ day,
General of Cavalry Bó Zhāo was sent to welcome the Empress Dowager from Dài.
The Emperor said:
"The Lü clan placed themselves as Chancellor of State,
and Lü Lù as Grand General,
arbitrarily dispatched General Guàn Yīng to attack Qí,
aiming to replace the Liú family.
Yīng remained at Xíngyáng and did not attack,
and conspired with the lords to eliminate the Lü clan.
Lü Chǎn planned evil activities,
Chancellor Chén Píng and Grand Marshal Zhōu Bó plotted to seize their army.
Zhūxū Marquis Liú Zhāng was the first to capture them.
The Grand Marshal personally led Xiāngpíng Marquis Tōng, holding an imperial edict, to enter the northern army camp.
Court Official Liú Jiē personally seized the seal from Zhao King Lü Lù.
Grand Marshal Bó received an additional ten thousand households,
and was granted five thousand catties of gold.
Chancellor Chén Píng and General Guàn Yīng each received three thousand households,
and two thousand catties of gold.
Zhūxū Marquis Liú Zhāng, Xiāngpíng Marquis Tōng, and Dōngmóu Marquis Liú Xīngjū each received two thousand households,
and a thousand catties of gold.
Court Official Jiē was enfeoffed as Yángxìn Marquis,
and granted a thousand catties of gold."
In December,
the Emperor said:
"Law is the standard of governance,
used to prohibit violence and guide good people.
Currently, once judged guilty,
innocent parents, wives, and siblings are implicated and punished,
tantamount to ransom collection,
which I do not approve of.
Let's discuss this."
The officials all said:
"People cannot govern themselves,
so laws were made to restrict them.
Collective punishment and implicating families,
serve to weigh heavily on their minds,
making them cautious of committing crimes again,
a practice from a long time ago.
It is suitable as it is now."
The Emperor said:
"I have heard that if the laws are just, people will be straightforward,
and if punishments are fair, people will comply.
Moreover, officials,
who are supposed to shepherd the people and guide them towards good,
yet, if they fail to do so,
and use unjust laws to punish them,
it instead harms the people and serves violence.
How can this be forbidden?
I do not see the advantage,
so who can make a plan?"
The officials all said:
"Your Majesty has bestowed great kindness,
your virtue surpasses greatly,
beyond what we ministers are capable of.
We request to follow the imperial order,
abolishing the collective punishment laws."
In January,
the officials said:
"Establishing the Crown Prince early
is the way to honor the ancestral temple.
We request the establishment of the Crown Prince."
The Emperor said:
"I lack virtue,
the spirits of heaven have not fully accepted offering,
and the people of the world have not expressed satisfaction.
Now, even if one cannot broadly seek wise and virtuous people nationwide to abdicate in their favor,
and say to establish a Crown Prince early,
it increases my lack of virtue.
What would it mean for the world?"
"Let it be settled as it is."
The officials said:
"Establishing the Crown Prince early,
is to emphasize the state and the temple's importance,
not to forget about the world."
The Emperor said:
"King Chǔ,
is my uncle,
elderly in years,
and well-versed in the principles of the world over time,
knowledgeable about the nation's great affairs.
King Wú,
is my brother,
benevolent and good-natured.
King Huáinán,
is my younger brother,
accumulating virtue to assist me.
How could they be displeased?
Among the vassal kings, imperial clan relations, and meritorious ministers,
there are many who are virtuous and righteous.
If we choose the virtuous to complement what I cannot accomplish,
it would be the spirit of the state,
and a blessing to the world.
Now, if we do not select from them,
but insist it must be a son,
people would consider me as ignoring the virtuous and solely favoring a son,
which is not how one should care for the world.
I fully do not agree."
The officials all strongly urged:
"In ancient times, the states of Yin and Zhou,
governed peacefully for over a thousand years each,
no one has exceeded this in governing the world,
by using this method.
Establishing an heir has always been a matter of the son.
Since long ago.
Emperor Gāo personally led the officials,
pacified the world at the beginning,
established marquises,
becoming the Great Ancestor as an emperor.
The princes and marquises were established as the ancestors of their states.
The descendants succeeding through generations unbroken,
is the great principle of the world,
thus Emperor Gāo established it to stabilize the realm.
Now to abandon the proper successor and select another from among the feudal lords and the imperial clan
is not the will of Emperor Gāo.
Further deliberation is inappropriate.
The son Mǒu is the eldest,
pure and sincere, kind and benevolent—
I request that he be established as Crown Prince."
The Emperor then approved it.
Thereupon, he granted one rank of nobility each to all commoners in the empire who were due to succeed their fathers.
He enfeoffed General Bó Zhāo as the Marquis of Zhǐ.
In the third month,
the officials requested the establishment of an Empress.
Empress Dowager Bó said:
"All the feudal lords are of the same surname,
so establish the Crown Prince's mother as Empress."
The Empress's surname was Dòu.
Because of establishing the Empress,

the Emperor bestowed cloth, silk, rice, and meat in set amounts to all widowers, widows, orphans, the childless, the impoverished, those aged eighty and above, and orphaned children aged nine and below across the empire.
The Emperor, having come from Dài,
upon newly ascending the throne,
bestowed virtue and kindness upon the empire,
pacifying the feudal lords and the barbarians of the four directions, all of whom were pleased.
Then he rewarded the meritorious officials who had followed him from Dài.
The Emperor said:
"When the high officials executed the various Lǚ and welcomed me,
I was hesitant,
and they all restrained me;
only the Commandant of the Central Guard Sòng Chāng urged me,
enabling me to preserve and serve the ancestral temple.
Having already honored Chāng as General of the Guards,
I now enfeoff him as the Marquis of Zhuàngwǔ.
As for the six who followed me,
their offices have all reached the Nine Ministers."
The Emperor said:
"The ranked marquises who followed Emperor Gāo into Shǔ and Hànzhōng, sixty-eight in all, shall each receive an additional fief of three hundred households.
Former officials of the two-thousand-picul rank and above who followed Emperor Gāo, such as Governor Zūn of Yǐngchuān and nine others, shall receive fiefs of six hundred households.
Governor Shēntú Jiā of Huáiyáng and nine others shall receive five hundred households.
Commandant Dìng of the Guards and nine others shall receive four hundred households.
Enfeoff Zhào Jiān, maternal uncle of the King of Huáinán, as the Marquis of Zhōuyáng,
and Sì Jūn, maternal uncle of the King of Qí, as the Marquis of Qīngguō."
In autumn,
he enfeoffed the former Chancellor of Chángshān, Cài Jiān, as the Marquis of Fán.
Someone advised the Right Chancellor, saying:
"You originally executed the various Lǚ,
welcomed the King of Dài,
and now you pride yourself on your merit,
accept high rewards from the Emperor,
and hold a respected position—
calamity will soon reach you."
The Right Chancellor, Bó, then pleaded illness and resigned,
and the Left Chancellor, Píng, solely became Chancellor.
In the tenth month of the second year,
Chancellor Píng passed away,
and again, the Marquis of Jiàng, Bó, was made Chancellor.
The Emperor said:
"I have heard that in ancient times, the feudal lords established states for over a thousand years,
each guarding their own lands,
presenting tribute in due season,
so the people were not burdened,
and high and low were joyful,
with no neglected virtue.
Now, many ranked marquises reside in Cháng'ān,
their fiefs are distant,
and the officials and soldiers bear the hardship and cost of transport,
while the marquises also have no means to instruct and guide their people.
Let the ranked marquises go to their states.
Those who are officials or are detained by imperial decree
shall send their crown princes."
At the end of the eleventh month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
On the fifteenth day of the twelfth month,
the sun was eclipsed again.
The Emperor said:
"I have heard that
Heaven gives birth to the multitude of people
and sets up a ruler for them to nurture and govern them.
If the ruler is without virtue,
and his governance is uneven,
then Heaven shows him disasters
to warn him of misrule.
Now at the end of the eleventh month,
there was an eclipse of the sun,
clearly seen in the sky—
what disaster could be greater!
I, who have been granted the preservation of the ancestral temple,
with my humble person placed above the myriad people as their sovereign,
the order or chaos of the empire
rests on me alone,
and only the two or three chief ministers are like my limbs.
If I, below, cannot properly nurture all living beings,
and above, bring disgrace to the brightness of the three luminaries,
my lack of virtue is great indeed.
Let this order reach all,
and let all ponder my faults and errors,
and what I fail to see or consider,
and be generous to inform me.
Also, recommend those who are virtuous, upright, and able to speak frankly and admonish severely,
to correct my shortcomings.
Moreover, each should diligently attend to their duties,
striving to reduce corvée and expenses for the convenience of the people.
Since I cannot extend virtue afar,
I am anxiously mindful that outsiders may have ill intentions,
hence defensive preparations have not ceased.
Now even if we cannot disband the border garrisons,
and we still strengthen troops for heavy defense,
let us disband the army of the General of the Guards.
The Grand Coachman shall retain only enough horses as are necessary,
and the rest shall be given to the relay stations."
In the first month,
the Emperor said:
"Agriculture is
the foundation of the empire.
Let the imperial field be opened,
and I myself will lead the plowing,
to supply the grain for the ancestral temple offerings."
In the third month,
the officials requested the establishment of the imperial sons as feudal kings.
The Emperor said:
"The King Yōu of Zhào died in captivity,
I deeply pity him,
and have already established his eldest son Suì as King of Zhào.
Suì's younger brother Pìqiáng, and the sons of King Dàohuì of Qí, the Marquis of Zhūxū, Zhāng, and the Marquis of Dōngmóu, Xīngjū, have merit,
and may be made kings."
Thereupon, he established the younger son of King Yōu of Zhào, Pìqiáng, as King of Héjiān,
established the Marquis of Zhūxū as King of Chéngyáng with the strategic comman dery of Qí,
established the Marquis of Dōngmóu as King of Jìběi,
the imperial son Wǔ as King of Dài,
the son Shēn as King of Tàiyuán,
and the son Yī as King of Liáng.
The Emperor said:
"In ancient times, to govern the empire,
there were banners at the court for presenting good advice,
and wooden boards for criticism,
to open the way of governance and attract remonstrators.
Now the law has crimes for criticism and seditious talk,
which makes the ministers dare not express their full feelings,
and the ruler has no way to hear of his faults.
How then can we attract the worthy and good from afar?
Abolish these laws.
If among the people, some curse the emperor in mutual agreements and later recant,
and officials consider it great treason,
or if they have other words,
and officials again consider it criticism,
this is the folly of the petty people's ignorance leading to death—
I greatly disapprove.
From now on,
those who commit such acts shall not be prosecuted."
In the ninth month,
for the first time, bronze tiger tallies and bamboo envoy tallies were made for the governors and chancellors of comman deries and states.
On the last day of the third month, the tenth month, Dīngyǒu,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
In the eleventh month,
the Emperor said:
"Previously, an edict was issued sending the ranked marquises to their states,
but some have made excuses and not gone.
The Chancellor is one I esteem;
let him lead the ranked marquises to their states for me."
The Marquis of Jiàng, Bó, was relieved as Chancellor and went to his state,
and the Grand Commandant, the Marquis of Yǐngyīn, Guàn Yīng, was made Chancellor.
The office of Grand Commandant was abolished,
and its duties were assigned to the Chancellor.
In the fourth month,
the King of Chéngyáng, Zhāng, passed away.
The King of Huáinán, Cháng, with his follower Wèi Jìng, killed the Marquis of Pìyáng, Shěnyǐjī.
In the fifth month,
the Xiōngnú invaded Běidì,
occupying Hé nán and raiding.
The Emperor first visited Gānquán.
In the sixth month,
the Emperor said:
"Hàn and the Xiōngnú have sworn to be as brothers,
not to harm the border regions,
which is why we have given much in tribute to the Xiōngnú.
Now the Wise King of the Right has left his territory,
leading his multitude to occupy the surrendered land in Hé nán,
without just cause,
coming and going near the frontier,
capturing and killing officials and soldiers,
driving away the barbarians protecting the frontier,
preventing them from dwelling in their former lands,
oppressing the border officials,
entering to plunder—
this is highly arrogant and unprincipled,
and contrary to the treaty.
Dispatch eighty-five thousand cavalry from the border officials to Gāonú,
and send the Chancellor, the Marquis of Yǐngyīn, Guàn Yīng, to attack the Xiōngnú."
The Xiōngnú withdrew,
and the Emperor dispatched the skilled officers of the Commandant of the Center to join the General of the Guards
and garrison Cháng'ān.
On the Xīnmǎo day,
the Emperor journeyed from Gānquán to Gāonú,
then proceeded to Tàiyuán,
where he met with his former officials,
bestowing gifts upon all of them.
He recognized achievements and distributed rewards,
granting oxen and wine to the people in the villages.
He exempted the people of Jìnyáng and Zhōngdū from taxes for three years.
He lingered and toured Tàiyuán for over ten days.
Jìběi King Liú Xīngjū, hearing that the Emperor was heading to Dài,
intending to campaign against the Hú,
rebelled,
mobilizing troops to attack Xíngyáng.
Thereupon, an edict was issued to dispatch the Chancellor's forces,
sending Jípú Hóu Chén Wǔ as Grand General,
leading a hundred thousand troops to attack him.
Qí Hóu Hè was appointed General,
stationed at Xíngyáng.
In the seventh month on the Xīnhài day,
the Emperor returned from Tàiyuán to Cháng'ān.
He then issued an edict to the officials, stating:
"Jìběi King has betrayed virtue and rebelled against his sovereign,
misleading officials and people,
committing great treason.
Jìběi officials and people who stabilize themselves before the troops arrive,
and those who surrender with their military territories and cities,
shall all be pardoned,
and restored to their official positions and titles.
Those who associated with King Xīngjū, coming and going,
shall also be pardoned."
In the eighth month,
the Jìběi army was defeated,
and its king was captured.
All Jìběi officials and people who had joined the king in rebellion were pardoned.
In the sixth year,
officials reported that Huáinán King Liú Cháng had abolished the laws of the previous emperor,
disobeyed the Son of Heaven's decrees,
lived without restraint,
conducted himself in a manner imitating the Son of Heaven,
arbitrarily enacted laws,
conspired with Jípú Hóu's heir, Qí, to rebel,
sent envoys to Mǐnyuè and the Xiōngnú,
mobilizing their troops,
intending to endanger the ancestral temple and state.
The officials deliberated,
all saying, "Cháng deserves public execution."
The Emperor could not bear to subject the king to the law,
pardoned his crimes,
but deposed him from his kingship.
The officials requested to place the king in Yándào, Shǔ, and Qióngdū,
and the Emperor consented.
Before Cháng reached his destination,
he fell ill and died on the journey,
and the Emperor pitied him.
Sixteen years later,
he posthumously honored Huáinán King Cháng with the title Lì King,
and enfeoffed his three sons as Huáinán King, Héngshān King, and Lújiāng King.
In the summer of the thirteenth year,
the Emperor said:
"I have heard that under the way of heaven, calamity arises from resentment, and blessings flourish from virtue.
The faults of the hundred officials
should rest with me.
Now the officials of secret prayers shift blame to subordinates,
highlighting my lack of virtue,
which I greatly disapprove of.
Let this practice be abolished."
In the fifth month,
Qí's Grand Granary Prefect Chúnyú Gōng, guilty and due for punishment,
was arrested and transported to Cháng'ān for imprisonment.
The Grand Granary Duke had no sons,
only five daughters.
As he was about to be taken away upon arrest,
he scolded his daughters, saying:
"To bear children but no sons,
in times of crisis, is of no use!"
His youngest daughter, Tíyíng, wept in sorrow,
and followed her father to Cháng'ān,
submitting a petition stating:
"My father served as an official,
and all in Qí praised his integrity and fairness.
Now he faces punishment for breaking the law.
I grieve that the dead cannot live again,
and the punished cannot be made whole;
even if one wishes to reform and start anew,
the path is blocked.
I am willing to be confiscated as a government slave,
to redeem my father's punishment,
allowing him to reform himself."
The petition reached the Son of Heaven,
who was moved and saddened by her intent,
and issued an edict:
"I have heard that in the time of Yǒuyúshì,
they distinguished clothing and caps with different patterns as punishment,
and the people did not offend.
Why was that?
Because governance was perfect.
Now the law includes three corporal punishments,
yet wrongdoing does not cease;
where does the fault lie?
Is it not that my virtue is thin and my teachings unclear?
I am deeply ashamed.
Thus, the guidance is impure, and the ignorant people fall into error.
The 'Book of Songs' says, 'The genial and respectful prince,
is the parent of the people.'
Now when people err,
punishment is applied before teaching is given,
so some who wish to reform and do good have no way to do so.
I deeply pity them.
Punishments that sever limbs,
scar skin and flesh,
causing lifelong suffering,
how painful and unvirtuous they are!
How can this be called the intent of being the people's parent?
Let corporal punishments be abolished."
The Emperor said:
"Agriculture
is the foundation of the world,
and no task is greater.
Now those who labor diligently in their work still bear the burden of land taxes,
which makes no distinction between the fundamental and the trivial,
and the way to encourage farming is incomplete.
Let the land taxes be abolished."
In the winter of the fourteenth year,
the Xiōngnú plotted to invade the border as raiders,
attacking Cháonáosài,
and killing the Běidì Commandant Áng.
The Emperor then sent three generals to station at Lǒngxī,
Běidì,
and Shàngjùn,
with Commandant of the Capital Zhōu Shě as Guard General,
and Chief of the Imperial Guard Zhāng Wǔ as Chariot and Cavalry General,
stationed north of the Wèi River,
with a thousand chariots,
and a hundred thousand cavalry. The Emperor personally inspected the troops,
drilled the soldiers, reiterated orders,
and rewarded the officers and men.
The Emperor wished to lead the attack against the Xiōngnú himself,
but the officials remonstrated,
and he did not listen.
The Empress Dowager firmly insisted to the Emperor,
and only then did he desist.
Thereupon, Dōngyáng Hóu Zhāng Xiàngrú was appointed Grand General,
Chéng Hóu Chì as Inner史,
and Luán Bù as General,
to attack the Xiōngnú.
The Xiōngnú fled.
In spring,
the Emperor said:
"I have been privileged to hold sacrificial animals and jade tokens to serve the Supreme Deity and the ancestral temple,
for fourteen years to this day,
a long span of time.
To have governed the world for so long despite my lack of acuity and clarity,
I am deeply ashamed.
Let the sacrificial grounds and jade tokens for various sacrifices be expanded.
In the past, the ancient kings gave generously without seeking reward,
offered sacrifices without praying for personal blessings,
honored the worthy over relatives,
put the people before themselves,
reaching the pinnacle of enlightenment.
Now I hear that the sacrificial officials in their prayers for blessings,
all dedicate them to my person,
not for the common people,
which shames me greatly.
With my lack of virtue,
to personally enjoy and独占 the blessings,
while the people do not share in them,
this compounds my lack of virtue.
Let the sacrificial officials pay respects,
without making any prayers."
At that time, Běipíng Hóu Zhāng Cāng was Chancellor,
and was clarifying the laws and calendar.
A man from Lǔ, Gōngsūn Chén, submitted a memorial discussing the cycle of the Five Virtues,
stating that now was the time of the Earth Virtue,
and the Earth Virtue should correspond to the appearance of a yellow dragon,
necessitating changes to the calendar, clothing colors, and systems.
The Son of Heaven referred the matter to the Chancellor for discussion.
The Chancellor deduced that it was currently the Water Virtue,
having just clarified the use of the tenth month as the start of the year and black as the color,
and considered his words incorrect,
requesting to dismiss the proposal.
In the fifteenth year,
a yellow dragon appeared in Chéngjì,
and the Son of Heaven summoned Lǔ's Gōngsūn Chén again,
appointing him as Erudite,
to elaborate on the Earth Virtue matter.
Thereupon, the Emperor issued an edict:
"A divine marvel has appeared in Chéngjì,
harmless to the people,
and the year has been abundant.
I will personally perform the suburban sacrifice to the Supreme Deity and various spirits.
Let the ritual officials deliberate,
without avoiding toil for my sake."
The ceremonial officials all said:
"In ancient times, the Son of Heaven personally conducted the sacrificial rites to the Supreme Deity at the outskirts during the summer,
hence it was called Jiao."
So the Son of Heaven first went to Yong,
to conduct the ceremony for the Five Emperors,
using the fourth month of Mengxia to fulfill the rites.
The Zhao man Xīn Yuánpíng observed the auspicious signs,
and persuaded the emperor to establish five temples at Weiyang.
He desired to produce the Zhou relics;
at that time, a jade blossom appeared.
In the sixteenth year,
the emperor personally performed the ceremony at the Weiyang temples of the Five Emperors,
also using summer rites, with an emphasis on the color red.
In the seventeenth year,
a jade cup was found,
engraved with "The ruler prolongs life."
Thus, the Son of Heaven began anew with the first year,
and decreed a grand feast throughout the land.
In that year,
Xīn Yuánpíng’s deeds were exposed,
and his three clans were executed.
Two years later,
the emperor said:
"As I am not enlightened,
I am unable to extend virtue far,
thus causing foreign lands occasionally not to rest in peace.
Indeed, outside the four wild borders, life is unstable,
while within the sacred territory, there is labor without peace.
The blame for these two aspects,
all lies in my meager virtue, unable to reach far.
Recently, for years,
the Xiongnu have invaded the borders,
killing many officials and citizens,
while border commanders and soldiers failed to clarify my internal intentions,
further highlighting my lack of virtue.
When conflict persists with drawn-out armies,
what will nations inside and outside do for peace?
Now I rise early and retire late,
laboring for the world,
grieving for the myriad people,
with constant fear and anxiety,
never once forgetting this in my heart,
thus sending messengers in constant succession,
forming connections along the roads,
to convey my intent to the Chanyu.
Now the Chanyu reverts to ancient ways,
planning the stability of state altars,
benefiting the myriad people's interests,
personally joining with me to overlook minor offenses,
and together abandon the docilities,
establishing the brotherhood bond,
thus preserving the simple folks in the world.
The peaceful relations have been established,
starting this year."
Six years later in winter,
thirty thousand Xiongnu entered Shangjun,
and thirty thousand entered Yunzhong.
Zhōngdàfū Lìngmiǎn was made General of Chariots and Cavalry,
stationed at Feihu;
Sū Yì, the former Chancellor of Chu, was made General,
stationed at Guanzhu;
General Zhāng Wǔ was garrisoned at Beidi;
Hénèi Prefect Zhōu Yǎfū was made General,
stationed at Xiliu;
Zōngzhèng Liú Lǐ was made General,
stationed at Bashang;
Lord Zhùzī had troops at Jímén;
prepared against the Hu.
After several months,
the invaders withdrew,
and the forces were disbanded.
The land experienced drought,
and locusts.
The Emperor extended grace:
ordered the lords not to send tribute,
relaxed mountain and marsh taxes,
reduced imperial use of dogs and horses,
decreased officials' numbers,
opened granaries to relieve the poor,
allowed the people to sell ranks.
Emperor Xiàowén came from Dai,
ascended the throne for twenty-three years,
neither adding to palaces, gardens, dogs, nor horses,
if any inconvenience,
immediately lifted it to benefit the people.
He once wanted to build a terrace,
summoned artisans for planning it,
costing a hundred gold.
The emperor said:
"A hundred gold is the livelihood of ten families,
